source.title: LLMs learn governing principles of dynamical systems, revealing an in-context neural scaling law
source.citation: To-Ni J. B. Liu et al., 2024
source.authors: To-Ni J. B. Liu; Nicolas Boulle; Raphael Sarfati; C. Earls

record.tranche_reason: The study discusses training neural scaling laws but measures a different relationship: in-context prediction loss versus the length of a time series in the prompt. It does not test the claim’s training-loss relationships or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The loss-curve results below concern in-context time-series prediction, not held-out pretraining loss against parameters, training tokens, or training compute. They therefore do not test V1–V7. Results comparing the study’s in-context predictions with baseline models are not results about the claim’s object.
record.test_reason: The study measures LLaMA-13b's in-context prediction loss against the length of the time series in the prompt. That is an inference-time, context-length relationship. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss against parameters, training tokens or compute. It does not test extrapolation across training runs, compute-optimal allocation, architecture shape, other training regimes, or downstream performance as a function of scale. Kaplan et al. are cited only to motivate an 'in-context' analogue. The remark that LLaMA-70b 'may achieve lower in-context loss' is qualitative and concerns in-context loss, not pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that LLaMA-2 models recover the transition rules of stochastic, chaotic and deterministic systems from in-context data without fine-tuning. They also conclude that in-context loss follows a power law in context length, an 'in-context neural scaling law', with Brownian and geometric Brownian motion plateauing early.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures loss from in-context time-series prediction as prompt context grows, using extracted transition distributions and Bhattacharyya distance or SDM; it does not reproduce training-loss scaling measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: For the study’s in-context results, Brownian and geometric Brownian motion plateau early, unlike the other systems; the authors connect this difference to stationarity. They also report that temperature changes the extracted distribution’s variance, and that T=0.7 gave better variance prediction in their temperature search.

fits_no_version.finding: In-context loss (Bhattacharyya or SDM) of LLaMA-13b falls roughly as a power law in context length for Markov chains, the noisy logistic map, the logistic map and Lorenz. Fitted exponents α are shown only in the Figure 20 legend. Brownian and geometric Brownian motion plateau near 10^2 context length, which the authors attribute to the lack of a stationary distribution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pretrained LLM's in-context prediction loss on dynamical-system time series decays as a power law in context length, except for non-stationary processes.

fits_no_version.finding: LLaMA-70b 'may achieve lower in-context loss' than LLaMA-13b on some systems, with no qualitative differences. For both models, in-context loss stops decreasing significantly for Markov chains with n≥9 states (Appendix A.3.3, Figure 14). This is in-context loss, not pretraining loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger pretrained LLMs attain modestly lower in-context loss on synthetic dynamical systems.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper notes that data leakage is not rigorously ruled out and that newer models such as LLaMA-3 were not evaluated. For the target claim, the central limitation is that the study measures in-context loss against prompt context length rather than the claimed training-scale relationships. Its loss curves are shown in figures, without uncertainty intervals stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Other reported distribution-shape and variance analyses do not measure the loss-versus-context relationship recorded here.

untested.parts: All: pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
All: extrapolation from small to large training runs.
All: depth/width effects at fixed parameter count.
All: power laws in other modalities or training regimes. In-context time-series learning is not a training regime.
All: downstream performance vs model scale or pretraining loss.
All: setup-dependence of training-law exponents or allocation.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to no version. The paper borrows the scaling-law framing but its independent variable is prompt length, not training scale. Baseline comparisons (Figures 8 and 21) are correctly left out as rows.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, training tokens, and training compute.
Extrapolation from small training runs to much larger runs.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power laws for training loss in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Setup-dependent training-loss exponents, compute-optimal splits, or departures from training-loss power laws.
